elections.research_note: contests 465 is metropolitan France only (matches the archive's count). Seats 546 from ord. 58-1065 art. 1 (source ord-58-1065): "465 pour les départements de la France métropolitaine ; 67 pour les départements algériens ; 4 pour les départements des Oasis et de la Saoura ; 10 pour les départements de la Guadeloupe, de la Guyane, de la Martinique et de le Réunion." So the 465 excludes Algeria (67), the Sahara (4), and the 10 DOM. Overseas territories (TOM) are not in 546. A Wikipedia-derived figure of 579 seats in the Assemblée (including 33 TOM members kept in office) is unverified and not used. Overseas split: the 1958 ordonnance counts seats, not circonscriptions, for Algeria and the Sahara, so no circonscription count is given for them. The persee quote is a 1959 journal summary, not the ordonnance text itself.

levels.note: Counted per canton. Until 2015, each département renewed half its cantons every three years, so each election before 2015 covers about half of France's cantons. Paris has no departmental election, and neither do the Lyon metropolis, Corsica, Guyane, or Martinique once their single authorities took over. The Sciences Po files for 1988 to 1998 cover metropolitan France only, so overseas cantons aren't counted for those years.
